incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: SLO alert - hosted decode p99 spike observed across multiple regions. Affected: streaming responses (stalling on continued token decode). Triggered at 17:02 UTC. Creating thread.

sam_oncall: on it. first pass: dashboards show p95 up ~200ms, p99 up ~1.2s over baseline for decode route. Streaming stalls visible as long gaps between chunks.

lina_runtime: I see it too. Not global but high-volume customer routes are showing the worst tail. Correlating with recent runtime deploy ~30m ago.

ben_compiler: which deploy? compiler/runtime or infra?

lina_runtime: runtime-worker: v3.14.2 rolled at 16:42 UTC. Build tag shows new decode kernel selection logic + updated compile flags for nvcc.

jess_sre: paging SLO: p99 must be < 350ms. Current p99 for decode=~1.6s in us-west-2. Impacting approximate 7% of requests but with high variance (stream stalls).

maria_cs: CS: two customers reported visible streaming stalls (chat app shows long pauses). They're asking if this is a regression from last night.

sam_oncall: quick mitigation ideas: 1) fallback model variant (smaller kernel) 2) revert runtime change on canary 3) force older compile flags in job definition. Which is fastest?

lina_runtime: revert on canary is fastest for safety. I can trigger a canary revert to v3.14.1 on a subset of pods. That should stop further rollouts and isolate.

ben_compiler: note: v3.14.2 enabled -use_fast_math nvcc flag and toggled a kernel that chooses between fused-attention and generic path. We benchmarked for throughput but didn't catch tail under low-util streaming. Could be precision/atomic ordering causing stalls on some SM configs.

sam_oncall: checking infra logs: attaching snippet:
```
[worker-42] decode kernel select: fused_attn_optimized -> loading kernel libdecode_v2.so
[worker-42] nvrtc compile flags: -O3 -use_fast_math -ftz
[worker-42] runtime: kcache miss, compiling JIT kernel
[worker-42] stall detected: 0.9s gap between token callbacks
```

jess_sre: env matrix: impacted nodes have driver 535.86 and CUDA 12.2. Not all nodes show problems. Could be interaction between driver and optimized kernel.

ben_compiler: that matches. On a few GPU models fused kernel uses different shared memory layout; -use_fast_math can change numerical ordering and some atomic loops rely on that behavior. Not typical but plausible.

lina_runtime: mitigation plan: 1) pause rollout -> done (deploy-bot confirmed). 2) revert canary to v3.14.1 on 10% of capacity -> I will flip now. 3) Add temporary route policy to send streaming decode to less-optimized variant (model_variant=stable_decode).

deploy-bot: rollback started: release v3.14.1 -> canary group (10%) at 17:12 UTC.

sam_oncall: I just toggled runtime route: fallback_variant=true for affected customer tokens via Console -> should bypass optimized kernel. Expect drop in throughput but reduced stalls.

maria_cs: telling customers we have a mitigation and rollback in progress. They want ETA.

jess_sre: quick customer impact estimate: ~120k streaming tokens in past 30m impacted; 3 customers reported UI stalls. No data exfiltration, just availability/latency.

ben_compiler: longer-term: we'll roll back the -use_fast_math change and add a hardware-specific guard for fused kernel selection. Also add p99 tail tests to CI that use low-throughput streaming scenarios.

lina_runtime: can we hotfix by disabling kernel selection for fused path at runtime flag? That would avoid full rebuild. I can push a runtime config toggle in ~20m.

sam_oncall: please do that as a stopgap while rollback completes. Add a config gate, then we can re-introduce optimized path behind an explicit opt-in per region.

lina_runtime: pushed runtime flag: env var DECODE_FORCE_GENERIC=1 on canary pods. Confirming logs show generic kernel chosen now.

policy-note(by sam_oncall): also enabling circuit-breaker to limit concurrent streaming sessions for impacted customers to reduce queueing: set max_concurrent_streams=8 for their orgs.

maria_cs: CS update posted to customer channel. They asked for status updates every 30m.

jess_sre: monitoring: p99 dropped from 1.6s -> 420ms on canary after flag. Need full rollback to restore baseline.

deploy-bot: rollback complete to v3.14.1 on 100% of that fleet at 17:36 UTC.

sam_oncall: post-rollback metrics: p95 back to normal; p99 improved to ~360-420ms. Still slightly above SLO in a couple AZs; investigating remaining tail.

ben_compiler: logging an internal issue: COMP-5873 with repro steps and kernel patch. Will coordinate with runtime for a safe re-roll once tests added.

lina_runtime: handing off to night on-call @ben_compiler for longer-term fix and to watch the remaining AZs. Sam, Jess — any followups?

sam_oncall: thanks. I'll keep an eye on alerts for 2 hours. If p99 spikes again -> escalate to infra.

jess_sre: I'll run a targeted smoke test across GPU types (A10G, A100 80GB, H100) overnight and post results in infra channel.

maria_cs: customers notified of rollback and mitigation. Offering post-mortem once root cause confirmed.

ben_compiler: taking handoff. summary for next on-call: root cause likely compile flag + fused kernel selection; mitigations applied: rollout paused, runtime flag forced to generic kernel, full rollback complete. Action items: add low-throughput streaming p99 tests, revert -use_fast_math in build, add hardware guard, re-run canary with extended tail tests.

sam_oncall: handing off thread. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-1457. Severity: P2. Linked: COMP-5873.
